# AI brief — Sunday 04 October 2026

## The day

David Robinson, who wrote the safety reports accompanying every major OpenAI model release, resigned this week and published an Atlantic editorial calling OpenAI's culture broken and arguing AI labs need nuclear-plant-level safeguards. This is the most operationally embedded safety critic to go public yet — not a policy hire but the person who produced the actual safety documentation. Separately, two low-signal stories from fringe outlets claim OpenAI fired three safety researchers over a leak; that claim has no corroboration from credible sources and should be treated with caution.

## How this was filtered

- 78 items pulled from 9 feeds in the last 30 hours
- 76 of those are about AI at all (2 matched no AI term as a whole word)
- 72 survived the noise filter (4 were stock listicles, task-force press releases or lifestyle filler)
- 54 distinct stories, once every rewrite of the same event is folded together
- 40 of those had not been reported here before (40 surfaced today in total), 11 more queued for the next run (capped at 40 a brief); 1091 headlines tracked in total
- Ordering is a deterministic score: release and legal language in the headline, a model version, how many independent outlets carried it, and whether the lab announced it itself. The model never chooses the order

### Feeds not used

- **AWS Machine Learning** — vendor how-to marketing rather than news; every item is a walkthrough of a service that shipped months ago
- **Anthropic** — publishes no RSS at all (/news/rss.xml is a 404) — covered via the Google News query instead
- **Hugging Face blog** — 862 items, almost all community tutorials; a release announcement is a needle in it and the noise gate cannot tell the difference from a title
- **Meta AI** — ai.meta.com/blog/rss/ returns HTTP 400
- **Microsoft AI** — blogs.microsoft.com/ai/feed/ returns HTTP 410 Gone
- **Reuters Technology** — HTTP 401 — the feed is behind their licensing wall
- **arXiv cs.AI** — 634 submissions a day is not news. Ranking them needs a different filter than this one and a model call per batch
